name: What is the difference between a modular and a stick-built backyard tiny home?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a modular and a stick-built backyard tiny home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Modular backyard tiny homes are largely constructed off-site in a factory setting, then transported and assembled on your property. This can often lead to faster construction times and reduced weather delays. Stick-built homes, conversely, are built entirely on-site from the ground up, offering greater design flexibility and customization to fit specific site challenges. Both methods result in durable, code-compliant structures; the choice often depends on budget, timeline, and design preferences.
acceptedAnswer.description: Modular homes are largely pre-built off-site for faster installation, while stick-built homes are constructed entirely on-site, offering more customization. Both are code-compliant.
